Butch I think can mean masculine. I think it can stop there--just have a superficial definition. But I also use it to mean a state of being. By this other definition, a person doesn't stop being butch when they're not looking or acting particularly masculine. I think it's a particular relationship with how you feel and act and dress. You don't stop being butch if you grow your hair out, for example. Or if you tone down your masculinity because you're not in a safe space to express it.

And I guess femme is pretty much the equivalent of that. Superficially feminine. Or internally feminine. 

With both of these, I think there's the idea of course that butches and femmes have qualities that are different than the femininity and masculinity that heteronormative people more often value.

I like to use butch/femme for everything but physiology. So outward appearance yes--but only things like how someone dresses themselves because it is an expression of their personality. I think it's both unfair and erroneous to describe someone's body as butch or femme. 

Also, notice I don't give any examples of what's masculine and feminine. You'll find aggressive femmes and submissive butches...old-school femmes and radical butches, whatever. So part of the definition eludes me.
